history.dynasty: Multiple - earliest shrine by tradition built by Vajranabha (Krishna's great-grandson); Gupta-period temple (Chandragupta II, c. 400 CE); present complex rebuilt in the 20th century (Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust, 1951)
history.summary: The Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi temple complex at Mathura is revered as the exact birthplace of Lord Krishna - the Garbha Griha (sanctum) stands over the prison cell where Devaki and Vasudeva were imprisoned by King Kansa. By tradition the first shrine was built by Krishna's great-grandson Vajranabha; a grand temple rose under the Guptas (c. 400 CE) and again c. 1150 CE, but the site suffered repeated destruction - by Mahmud of Ghazni (1017-18), Sikandar Lodi (16th century), and Aurangzeb (1669), who erected the Shahi Eidgah mosque adjacent to the site, which still stands. The land was auctioned by the East India Company in 1815 and bought by Raja Patnimal of Benares; in 1944 Madan Mohan Malaviya repurchased it with Jugal Kishore Birla's help, the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust was formed in 1951 (now Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan), and the new complex - Keshavdev Temple, Garbha Griha shrine, Bhagavata Bhavan and Potra Kund - was completed in February 1982 with Jaidayal Dalmia overseeing construction. Entry is free; photography is restricted inside the complex.

name: Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi
town_description: Mathura is an ancient city on the banks of the Yamuna in the Braj region, revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna and counted among Hinduism's Sapta Puri (seven holy cities). A major pilgrimage centre for millennia, it is dotted with temples, ghats and kunds, and lies about 160 km south-east of Delhi on the Delhi-Agra corridor.

travel.airport: Agra Airport (Kheria), about 75 km away; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 160 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction, a major railhead, a few kilometres from the complex.
travel.road: On Deeg Marg near Deeg Gate Chouraha; well connected by road to Delhi (NH-19) and Agra; local autos and taxis available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami (August/September) draws the biggest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer (April-November): 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-9:30 PM; winter (November-April): 5:30 AM-12:00 PM and 3:00-8:30 PM; Garbha Griha darshan runs through the day (per tourtravelworld.com - verify locally). Entry free; photography restricted inside the complex.
